f.title: Include the standard headings in line listings
f.statement: A line listing provides key information on individual cases, with reactions classified by body system for the most serious presenting sign or symptom. Headings usually included are: country of occurrence (if relevant); source; age and gender of participant; dose(s) of suspected medicine(s); dosage form and/or route, batch number when applicable; duration of treatment and time to onset; description of reaction as reported; patient outcome; and comment (if relevant).
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

f.title: Classify seriousness using the SAE criteria and medical judgement
f.statement: A serious adverse event is any untoward occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening (at risk of death at the time of the event), requires or prolongs hospitalisation, results in a congenital anomaly/birth defect, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or is a medically significant/important event. Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised to decide whether other situations are serious, such as events that may jeopardise the patient or require intervention to prevent a listed outcome.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

rows.actor: Sponsor / applicant of the clinical trial

Such instances could include medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation, but which may jeopardise the patient or may require intervention to prevent one of the outcomes listed in the definition above.
rows.review_note: Review: statement summarises the SAE criteria of the same section; quote proves the medical-judgement duty. Double-check: below 90 because the criteria list is outside the quote.

f.title: Assess expectedness against the PI or investigator's brochure, treating unlabelled fatal outcomes as unexpected

A reaction whose outcome is not consistent with the medicine information should be considered unexpected, and an expected ADR with a fatal outcome should be considered unexpected unless the South African labelling specifically states that it might be associated with a fatal outcome.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

rows.quote: The sponsor/applicant of a clinical trial in South Africa is responsible for the submission of an annual Development Safety Update Report [ICH E2F] that includes information gathered from all clinical experience with the IP, whether in SA or elsewhere. Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) should be submitted within one year from approval of the study and annually thereafter.
rows.review_note: Review: "is responsible" sets the level; timing sentence uses should. Double-check: confirmed.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Annual DSUR (first within one year from study approval, then annually)

f.title: Include the required items in each six-monthly progress report
f.statement: Any trial lasting more than 6 months must submit regular progress reports, starting 6 months after trial approval and six-monthly thereafter until the final report, including: SAHPRA study tracking number and protocol number; study title; the IP; sponsor and applicant details; trial information; participant enrolment; line listing of local SAEs and SUSARs including deaths; any other item specified at protocol approval; any safety issue of special concern outside South Africa; line listing of all critical and major protocol violations at the site; and signatures of the national PI and the applicant/sponsor representative.
f.applicability: Trials of more than 6 months' duration

rows.quote: SAHPRA requires that any trial of more than 6 months duration must submit regular progress reports, starting from 6 months after the trial approval and six monthly thereafter until the final report that details the progress of the trial, which must include inter alia: a) SAHPRA study tracking number and Protocol number b) Study title c) The investigational product (IP) d) Details of sponsor and applicant e) Trial information f) Participant enrolment g) Line listing of local serious adverse events and suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions (SUSARS), including deaths h) Any other item specified during the SAHPRA approval of the protocol application i) Any safety issue of special concern outside South Africa j) Line listing of all critical and major protocol violation at the site k) Signatures of national PI and representative of Applicant/Sponsor

f.title: Agree any alternative blind-preserving reporting format with SAHPRA
f.statement: SAHPRA may request unblinding where there are significant safety concerns. If the sponsor is concerned that unblinding adverse events will compromise study integrity, it can propose an alternative reporting format that maintains the blind, which must be agreed by SAHPRA.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

f.title: Report pregnancy- and breastfeeding-related ADRs per Table 1 regardless of contraindication
f.statement: The sponsor/applicant must report suspected ADRs related to pregnancy or breastfeeding as specified in section 6.2, regardless of whether the drug is contraindicated in pregnancy and/or lactation.
f.clause: 7.5 Reports Relating to Pregnancy and Breast-Feeding
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

f.title: Wait for the pregnancy outcome and do not report pregnancies with no foetal effect
f.statement: Pregnancy reports should not be forwarded before the outcome is known, unless unintended pregnancy is suspected as an ADR, and should not be submitted if there is no adverse effect on the foetus/infant.
f.clause: 7.5 Reports Relating to Pregnancy and Breast-Feeding

f.title: Report overdoses associated with an SAE per Table 1
f.statement: Overdoses should be reported when associated with a serious adverse event, according to section 6.2, regardless of whether they were intentional or accidental.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Specify whether an overdose was intentional or accidental
f.statement: When reporting an overdose, whether it was intentional or accidental must be specified.

f.title: Define the safety reporting period in the protocol and application, and notify SAHPRA of delayed SAEs
f.statement: The duration of safety reporting for a clinical trial should be defined in the protocol and the clinical trial application form and approved by SAHPRA. If a delayed SAE is identified that would affect participants who received the IP, SAHPRA should be notified so that participants can be followed up.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

f.title: Route post-marketing study ADRs to the Vigilance Unit and comparator/concomitant ADRs to the Clinical Trials Unit
f.statement: ADRs occurring during post-marketing studies (Phase 4 and observational studies) should be reported to SAHPRA's Vigilance Unit; ADRs occurring during use of concomitant and/or comparator medicines in a clinical trial should be reported to SAHPRA's Clinical Trials Unit.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

Adverse Drug Reactions occurring during the use of concomitant and/or comparator medicine in a clinical trial should be reported to the Clinical Trials Unit of SAHPRA.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed against the source.

f.title: Send clinical trial safety information, post-marketing study reports and Section 21 SAEs to the designated SAHPRA mailboxes
f.statement: Reportable safety information under clinical trials must be sent to SAHPRA's designated clinical trial SAE mailbox; reportable safety information for post-marketing studies must be sent to the ADR mailbox; SAEs for medicines used under Section 21 are sent to the Section 21 mailbox (addresses in section 8.1).
f.clause: 8.1 Safety Reporting Requirements, Where to Submit a Report
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines

f.title: Include the required administrative and clinical data in initial expedited SUSAR reports
f.statement: Within 7 or 15 days (per section 6.2), a complete initial expedited SUSAR report with the required administrative and clinical data must be submitted, including: SAHPRA study reference number and protocol number; the suspected IP; an identifiable participant (e.g. participant code); an adverse event assessed as serious and unexpected with a reasonable suspected causal relationship; an identifiable primary reporting source; the identity of the sender; and other comments or background information.
f.clause: Annexure A: Required Information, 1. Initial Expedited SUSAR reports
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Submit the follow-up/final expedited report eight days after the initial report with the required content
f.statement: Eight days after the initial safety report, a complete follow-up/final expedited report with the required administrative and clinical data is submitted, containing: a copy of/information from the initial report; administrative and identification information (case identification, primary source(s), sender and receiver); and case information (patient characteristics, reactions/events with time to reaction, relevant tests and procedures, IP information, and a narrative case summary with further information).
f.clause: Annexure A: Required Information, 2. Follow-up/Final Expedited Report
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Use the SAHPRA SAE reporting form, preferably typed, with the required fields
f.statement: The SAHPRA SAE reporting form (Annexure B) should preferably be typed and covers: administrative details (study title, protocol number, SAHPRA reference number); site information; participant information (trial ID, age, gender, relevant history); SAE information (report type initial/follow-up/final, onset and stop dates, outcome, description, causality, dechallenge/rechallenge, management); suspected medicine information (IP, concomitant/comparator medicines, route, dose, indication, start dates, therapy duration); final outcome; applicant contact details; and the name, designation and signature of the person completing the form.
f.applicability: Clinical trials approved by SAHPRA using registered or unregistered medicines
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety system configuration
